angle_name: Exact-telescoping sieve hybrid: Heath-Brown/Harman decomposition of the prime measure in the dual pairing, with sieve weights used only as a lossless change of basis (never as majorants), reducing the Abel face to bilinear Gram sums of M-samples plus a self-similar renewal edge
mechanism: Swap the Abel sum to its dual: S = M(K)R(y) + Σ_{y<n≤x} 1_P(n)·M(x/n) − ∫_y^x M(x/t) dt/log t + O(floor corrections), so μ now enters through Mertens samples M(x/n) paired against the prime indicator minus its logarithmic density. Decompose 1_P on (y,x] by Heath-Brown's identity (or a Harman-sieve schedule) at level D = x^δ: every piece is either type I — a weight of convolution form (g*1) with g supported on [1,D] — or type II bilinear with both variables in [x^η, x^{1−η}]. The NEW leverage is a telescoping lemma: for ANY weight of the form (g*1), Σ_{n≤X} (g*1)(n)·M(X/n) = Σ_{a≤D} g(a) EXACTLY, because Σ_{b≤Z} M(Z/b) = 1 (i.e., μ*1 = δ applied along the hyperbola). Upper/lower sieve weights λ± = Σ_{d|n, d≤D} λ_d are themselves of this (g*1) form, so all type-I and sieve-weight pairings evaluate with zero loss — no |M|, no M² moments, no triangle inequality, full sign interaction retained — and their exact values cancel against the corresponding Li-integral pieces using only unconditional PNT/Vinogradov–Korobov inputs. Crucially, parity is confronted rather than evaded: the sieve is never used as a one-sided positivity device (which parity blocks for prime detection); it is used as an exact basis change, so the parity ambiguity is localized, undamaged, into the type-II region. What survives is (a) a bounded set of dyadic bilinear blocks B(M₀,N₀) = Σ_{m~M₀}Σ_{n~N₀} a_m b_n M(x/(mn)) with divisor-bounded coefficients — structurally the same object as the repo's projectedRenewalGramValue (windowed Gram of signed M-samples), so the Abel face is transported onto quadratic-face-shaped statements rather than onto 𝔉-class moment bounds; and (b) an edge term from restricting n > y: extending each type-I piece to all n ≤ x for telescoping leaves Σ_{a} g(a)·Σ_{b≤y/a} M((x/a)/b), and the truncated hyperbola sum Σ_{b≤√X} M(X/b) is exactly the dual of the original Abel functional at the smaller scale X = x/a. This self-similarity yields a renewal inequality T(x) ≤ Σ_a |g(a)|·(1 + T(x/a)·scale-factor) + (bilinear blocks), which is legitimately inductive (scale strictly drops, a ≥ 2) and matches the project's renewal framing. Honest summary: this is a reduction/alignment mechanism — it proves the two faces meet through sieve combinatorics — plus an unconditional rung-0/1 candidate from the regions where exact telescoping and unconditional M-savings apply; it does not by itself supply the missing √-cancellation input.
new_leverage: The exact telescoping lemma Σ_{n≤X}(g*1)(n)·M(X/n) = Σ_a g(a), applied to sieve weights λ± and all type-I pieces: a lossless evaluation of sieve-weighted Mertens pairings that uses no M² moments, no Cauchy–Schwarz, and no absolute values — by construction outside the 𝔉-closure class for the type-I/main-term part. Second, the observation that the restricted-range edge is the SAME Abel functional at scale x/a, giving a renewal recursion aligned with ProjectedRenewalQuadraticBoundedStatement instead of a loss.
target_estimate: Bilinear Gram remainder bound (the named estimate this angle reduces the target to): for every dyadic pair (M₀,N₀) with M₀N₀ ≍ x, x^η ≤ M₀ ≤ x^{1/2}, and coefficients |a_m| ≤ τ₃(m), |b_n| ≤ τ₃(n) log n arising from Heath-Brown's identity at level D = x^δ (δ, η small fixed, e.g. δ = η = 1/10): B(M₀,N₀) := Σ_{m~M₀} Σ_{n~N₀} a_m b_n M(⌊x/(mn)⌋) ≪_ε x^{1/2+ε}, uniformly over the O(log² x) blocks; combined with the exact type-I telescoping (loss O(D) = O(x^δ) absorbed by δ < 1/2) and the renewal edge inequality iterated O(log log x) times, this yields the Abel face |Σ_{d≤K} μ(d)R(⌊x/d⌋)| ≪_ε x^{1/2+ε'} with ε' = ε + O(δ). Losses: x^ε from divisor-bounded coefficients and piece count; the induction multiplies constants by O(Σ_a |g(a)|/a)-type factors per level, controlled if the renewal kernel has mass < 1 (unverified).

obstacle_positions.F_closure: Type-I and sieve-weight pieces exit the class by construction: the telescoping identity uses mu*1 = delta exactly, with zero M-squared-moment input and no triangle/CS recombination; the mu-times-prime sign interaction is carried intact. The type-II bilinear blocks are NOT claimed to exit the class — if they are then bounded by CS plus M-squared moments the exponent expands exactly as the audit predicts; the reduction's content is that any non-F input needs to be supplied only on Gram-shaped blocks, i.e., on the target's own quadratic face, not on a new object.
obstacle_positions.fiber_growth: No pair-to-modulus transfer to reduced denominators is used anywhere, so the exact counterexample does not apply in these coordinates. An analogous question reappears as collision multiplicity of floor(x/(mn)) across (m,n) in a block; fibers there are divisor-bounded (x^epsilon for typical values) except in the degenerate region mn ~ x where floor values are O(1) but M is O(1) too — believed benign, unverified, and flagged as the place obstacle 2 could re-materialize.
obstacle_positions.pinned_vs_averaged: The telescoping identity is an exact integer identity at the pinned x — no averaging, no exceptional sets, fully immune. The bilinear blocks remain pinned; if the quadratic-face side is ultimately proved by block-averaged estimates, the exceptional-set risk transfers there intact. Honestly: partially addressed (main terms), inherited (remainder).
obstacle_positions.modulus_magnitude: Inapplicable: the mechanism uses no wheel or primorial modulus; the only auxiliary parameter is the sieve level D = x^delta, polynomial in x. Nothing here relies on square-root-of-modulus gains.
obstacle_positions.parity: Confronted head-on, per the assigned lens: upper/lower sieve weights appear ONLY inside the exact telescoping (a change of basis), never as one-sided majorants of primes, so no positivity fudge is committed — the classical parity wall obstructs nonnegative prime detection, and this mechanism never attempts detection. The parity ambiguity is transported, undiluted, into the type-II blocks, where the needed statement is signed cancellation of a mu-linear pairing — a statement class parity heuristics do not forbid. The wall is thus localized, not breached; breaching it is exactly the quadratic face.
obstacle_positions.circularity: No pointwise bound stronger than unconditional Landau/Vinogradov-Korobov is used on R or M anywhere; the d=1 danger sits in the boundary M(K)R(y), which the packet declares separately self-consistent. The renewal edge uses the SAME functional at strictly smaller scale x/a with a ≥ 2, which is legitimately inductive provided the base case and kernel mass are unconditional — this is the one place a hidden RH-strength assumption could sneak in, and I flag the kernel-mass condition as the audit point.
obstacle_positions.finite_range: All identities are exact integer identities checkable symbolically and numerically without extrapolation; numerics are used only as falsifiers (the kill test) and to select delta, eta. The flat 0.35-0.43 coefficient is used only to predict which bilinear blocks should already show cancellation in range — no promotion from the calibration regime, explicitly remembering it is the Mertens-conjecture trap regime.

kill_test: Two-stage, both cheap. (1) Integer identity check (hours): at x = 10^6, verify Σ_{n≤X}(g*1)(n)M(X/n) = Σ_a g(a) exactly for Heath-Brown's actual coefficient arrays and for a beta-sieve lambda-plus/minus at D = x^{1/10}, including the floor-corrected restricted-range bookkeeping — any mismatch kills the mechanism's core. (2) Block-growth test (a day of compute): at x = 10^6, 10^7, 10^8, compute every dyadic bilinear block B(M0,N0) from the decomposition and fit the growth exponent of Σ_blocks |B| in x; if the exponent is ≥ 0.75 (no gain over the direct triangle scale) or the per-block cancellation coefficient |B|/sqrt(ΣΣ M(x/mn)^2) grows with x, the reduction transports the difficulty without reducing it — killed. Also compute the renewal-kernel mass Σ_a |g(a)|·(x/a-scale weight); if it exceeds 1 the induction diverges — killed.
rung0_plan: Unconditional product-savings bound: S ≪ x·exp(−c(log x)^{3/5−ε}), with the savings factor strictly better than any termwise triangle bound because it is a PRODUCT of two independent unconditional savings. Route: dual form S = M(K)R(y) + Σ_{y<p≤x} M(x/p) − Li-integral; the boundary term carries doubled VK savings outright (product of M and R factors, each ≪ t·exp(−c(log t)^{3/5}(log log t)^{−1/5})); for the core, expand R via the explicit formula with the Vinogradov–Korobov zero-free region and pair each zero term x^rho with the Möbius Dirichlet partial sum Σ_{d≤K} μ(d)d^{−rho}, which has its own unconditional exp(−c√log K) savings uniformly for |Im rho| in the relevant range — the product of zero-region savings and Möbius-sum savings beats every termwise bound by the second factor. Deliverable is bounded-effort classical analytic number theory (no new ideas needed beyond uniformity bookkeeping in the ordinate aspect) and is o of the honest trivial scale derived from termwise VK bounds.
plausible_partial: Named partial, plausibly provable at bounded effort and formalizable: the Renewal Reduction Lemma — an exact identity plus inequality showing the Abel functional T(x) := |Σ_{d≤K} μ(d)R(⌊x/d⌋)| satisfies T(x) ≤ Σ_{a≤D} |g(a)|·(1 + c_a·T(x/a)) + Σ_blocks |B(M0,N0)| + O(x^{1/2+δ}) unconditionally, i.e., a machine-checkable bridge showing the Abel face is controlled by (its own smaller-scale copies) + (windowed Gram sums of M-samples of exactly the projectedRenewalGramValue shape). This would be a formalization-support result aligning the two kernel-equivalent faces through explicit sieve combinatorics, in the spirit of the repo's existing connecting-equivalence work, and independently the rung-0 product-savings bound S ≪ x·exp(−c(log x)^{3/5−ε}) as a standalone unconditional estimate.
self_assessed_risk: High overall; stated plainly, my weakest assumption is that the type-II bilinear Gram blocks are genuinely easier than the Abel sum itself — the exact telescoping may only relocate the sign interaction rather than weaken the difficulty, in which case the reduction is aesthetically clean but a net zero on the frontier. Second weakest: the restricted-range edge is the same functional at scale x/a, and the renewal induction converges only if the kernel mass condition holds (unverified; if it fails, the edge term is rung-2-fatal since its trivial size is x^{1+o(1)}·exp(−c√log x)). Probabilities (honest guesses, UNVERIFIED): telescoping identity survives stage-1 kill test ~90%; block-growth test shows a real exponent gain ~30-40%; renewal reduction lemma provable and formalizable at bounded effort ~50%; rung-0 product-savings bound provable ~60%; this angle reaching rung 2 unaided: very low (<5%) — its realistic value is alignment of the two faces plus a rung-0/1 unconditional result.
